newsitem.title: USA: Argentine telecom ADRs rise, boosted by U.S. bonds.
newsitem.headline: Argentine telecom ADRs rise, boosted by U.S. bonds.

text.p: Argentine telecommunications companies' American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) jumped on Friday, boosted by a rally in the U.S. Treasury 30-year bond, traders said.

ADRs in Telefnica de Argentina were up 3/4 to 32-1/2. Volume was 2.1 million ADRs in mid-afternoon, more than twice the daily level, and the company was among the most active on the New York Stock Exchange.
Telecom Argentina rose 1-7/8 to 49-1/4 in moderate trade.

Rate changes tend to affect Latin American shares since investors have often switched out of regional stocks when U.S. interest rates rise. Argentine stocks are especially sensitive to changes in U.S. interest rates, since the local currency is pegged to the dollar.
Traders said the rally in the long bond had helped Argentine stocks and telecommunications ADRs in particular. They are highly liquid shares popular with investors seeking exposure in Argentina.
"That's going to give a trend to the upside," a trader said.
The 30-year bond was up 25/32 to yield 6.82 in midafternoon. It was helped by U.S. jobs and wages data that eased worries the Federal Reserve would increase rates.
The ADRs were also helped by the rise in the New York Stock Exchange and by demand from Argentine pension funds.
Among other Argentine stocks, Banco Francs rose 7/8 to 29-5/8, Banco de Galicia rose 54/64 to 24-55/64 and oil company YPF was up 1/4 to 26-3/4.
